textbookText: A. Tick the correct alternatives: 1. What does the term "vegetation" refer to in a general sense? a. Animal life b. Plant life c. Soil composition d. Atmospheric conditions

2. Why cultivated crops and fruits are not considered part of natural vegetation? a. They are too small b. They are not found in Nepal c. They require human intervention d. They are not useful for wildlife habitat
3. At what altitude range does the Temperate Coniferous Evergreen Forest grow in Nepal? a. 1000 to 2000 m b. 2000 to 3000 m c. 3000 to 4000 m d. 4000 to 5000 m

4. What is the primary goal of In-situ conservation, such as national parks in Nepal? a. To promote agriculture b. To protect endangered species in their natural habitats c. To facilitate botanical research d. To establish zoological gardens
5. According to the joint survey conducted between 2067 to 2071 BS, what percentage of Nepal's landmass is covered by forests? a. 29.83% b. 44% c. 39.1% d. 12.1%
6. How does deforestation contribute to soil erosion? a. By promoting soil fertility b. By decreasing overland flow c. By enhancing water infiltration d. By worsening soil erosion
7. What is the primary purpose of botanical gardens in Nepal? a. To cultivate crops b. To serve as wildlife reserves c. To preserve genes of endangered species d. To provide timber resources

8. What is the primary role of seed banks in preserving plant species? a. To promote seed production b. To ensure a constant supply of herbs c. To safeguard seeds outside their natural habitats d. To facilitate soil erosion
9. How does deforestation affect the climate? a. It has no impact on climate b. It improves rainfall patterns c. It leads to ecological imbalances d. It enhances oxygen levels
10. Which conservation method involves growing trees along with crops on less productive farmland? a. Afforestation b. Community Forests c. Agroforestry d. Modern Pest Control Techniques

B. Answer the following questions: 1. Define vegetation. Write one essential role of vegetation in the biosphere. 2. What is the altitude range of Alpine Vegetation in Nepal? 3. What is the main influence on the natural vegetation in Nepal? 4. What role does vegetation play in erosion control? 5. What is the primary goal of In-situ conservation? 6. Which bio-climatic zone in Nepal is characterized by Subtropical Forest? 7. What is the significance of protected areas in Nepal for biodiversity? 8. Describe the importance of vegetation in influencing soil characteristics. 9. List and briefly describe the types of natural vegetation in Nepal based on altitude. 10. Discuss the economic importance of vegetation in relation to the world economy. 11. Describe two types of conservation methods. 12. Briefly explain the importance of botanical gardens. 13. Differentiate between in-situ and ex-situ conservation of biodiversity. 14. Explain the concept of seed banks and their importance. 15. What is deforestation? Describe the causes, consequences of deforestation in the context of Nepal and suggest possible mitigating measures.

Project Work 1. Prepare a research-based report on national and international efforts on nature conservation. Use trustworthy online sources, news articles, and magazines to discover how our world is being protected. And present in your class to inspire each other.

2. Plan a field trip together to visit a nearby botanical garden or seed bank (if there's one nearby). During the trip, observe and learn about ex-situ conservation efforts firsthand. Pay close attention to how plants' genetic resources are collected, preserved, and used to conserve biodiversity and promote sustainable agriculture.
